title: Algebraicity and smoothness of the stack of all nodal curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. On $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] let $\mathfrak C$ be the category fibred in groupoids of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces with geometric fibres of dimension at most one, with $T$-isomorphisms as arrows in a fibre and cartesian pullback. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). A stack means that isomorphisms form an etale sheaf and all etale descent data for objects are effective; an algebraic stack is such a stack with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas representable by algebraic spaces. Then $\mathfrak C$ is an algebraic stack. Its full subcategory $\mathfrak N$ of families with nonempty geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension] and at worst nodal geometric singularities is an open algebraic substack, smooth over $k$. Here an ordinary geometric node is a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] with completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over the algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. No connectedness condition is imposed. An open substack pulls back along every scheme-valued object to an open subscheme of its base. Smoothness of a morphism representable by algebraic spaces is checked on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and smoothness of a stack over $k$ means that the composite of a smooth scheme atlas with its structure morphism is smooth. These conclusions hold after every field extension of $k$.

proof.text: Work first over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and write $\mathcal C$ for the same groupoid of families over all schemes. By [lem-sfb-curve-descent-isom-spaces] it is an fppf stack, hence an etale stack, and its isomorphism sheaves are algebraic spaces, which is precisely representability of its diagonal. The cardinal bound in Artin\'s criterion is satisfied: over each finite type field, finite-presentation algebraic spaces and arrows have presentations by finitely many affine charts and finitely many ring equations and maps; the chosen scheme universe bounds these sets of presentations [def-weil-size-convention]. This size verification does not assert effectivity or an atlas.

Apply [lem-sfb-artin-representable-diagonal-criterion] over $\mathbf Z$. Its stack, diagonal, and size assumptions were checked in step 1. Limit preservation, including descent and eventual equality of arrows, is [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation]. The pushout equivalence [lem-sfb-curve-infinitesimal-pushout] applies in particular to the Artinian pushouts in the criterion, giving (RS). The two finite-dimensional vector spaces required there are exactly those in [lem-sfb-curve-tangent-finiteness]. Every formal object is effective by [lem-sfb-curve-formal-effectivity]; its statement imposes no restriction on the residue field, so it covers the required finite type ones. Openness of versality with the same Artinian lifting definition is [lem-sfb-curve-openness-versality]. Every premise of the criterion is therefore met, and $\mathcal C$ has a representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas.

source.place: Tag 0D5A (theorem-curves-algebraic), absolute case, with the separately stated tangent-space Tag 0D57.

proof.text: The groupoid $\mathfrak C$ is the 2-fibre product $\mathcal C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}k$: an object is a family over $T$ together with its structural map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and the arrows on both sides are the same cartesian isomorphisms. Pull back an atlas $U\to\mathcal C$ to the scheme $U_k$. Its diagonal tests are base changes of the algebraic-space Isom sheaves, hence algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its atlas is smooth and surjective: smoothness on scheme charts is preserved by base change by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], after using the locally constant relative dimension in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] to cover each smooth chart by fixed-dimension opens. Surjectivity persists because a nonempty fibre over a field remains nonempty after a field extension (a tensor product of nonzero vector spaces over a field is nonzero). Thus $\mathfrak C$ is algebraic.

For any $X\xrightarrow f T$ in $\mathfrak C$, let $V\subseteq X$ be the maximal nodal relative-dimension-one open of [lem-sfb-space-nodal-locus-base-change]. Put $Z=|X|\setminus|V|$ and $T_{\mathrm{nod}}=T\setminus|f|(Z)$. Properness, which includes universal closedness, makes this an open subscheme. It consists exactly of the base points over which the entire geometric fibre lies in $V$. It is compatible with arbitrary base change: $V$ pulls back by the cited lemma, its complement therefore pulls back, and the image of that complement pulls back on point sets. Indeed over a point $t'$ above $t$, a nonempty bad fibre over $\kappa(t)$ stays nonempty over $\kappa(t')$, since tensoring a nonzero field-valued point with a field extension is faithfully flat; an empty bad fibre stays empty. Thus a base change has all its fibres empty or pure one-dimensional and at worst nodal if and only if its base map factors through $T_{\mathrm{nod}}$.

source.place: Tag 0DSY (lemma-nodal-curves), proof: complement of the proper image of the bad locus.

proof.text: The locus $T_{\ne\varnothing}=|f|(|X|)$ of nonempty fibres is open by [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open], and is also closed by properness. Its formation commutes with base change by the same nonempty-field-fibre argument in step 4. Consequently $T_N=T_{\mathrm{nod}}\cap T_{\ne\varnothing}$ is open, commutes with all base changes, and a map $T'\to T$ factors through it exactly when the pulled-back family lies in $\mathfrak N$. These opens give the scheme pullbacks of $\mathfrak N\to\mathfrak C$, so this is an open immersion of stacks. Explicitly descent follows by restricting descent in $\mathfrak C$ to these compatible opens. Pulling $\mathfrak N$ back to the scheme atlas $U_k$ restricts it to an open scheme atlas, and its Isom sheaves are the same as those of $\mathfrak C$, so $\mathfrak N$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 0DSY; nonempty-fibre refinement using spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S.

proof.text: Let $C/\Omega$ be any geometric fibre of a family in $\mathfrak N$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. It is a separated finite-type algebraic space of dimension one, hence a scheme by [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme]. It is pure of dimension one by hypothesis and proper and of finite type. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion]: every closed point is smooth or an ordinary node by our geometric-fibre hypothesis, so $C$ is a local complete intersection and its first-Fitting singular scheme $Z_C$ is unramified over $\Omega$. Its underlying closed subset is the nonsmooth locus by [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus], applied with $d=1$; flatness holds over the field, local finite presentation comes from the given family, and the required geometric purity is exactly the nodal-fibre hypothesis, which tests all algebraically closed extensions.

source.place: Tag 0E00 (lemma-nodal-curves-smooth), inclusion in lci+, using curves.tex Tag 0C4E.

proof.text: The scheme $C$ is Noetherian: it is quasi-compact because it is of finite type over a field, and is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since a field is Noetherian. The closed subscheme $Z_C$ is locally of finite type over $\Omega$ (its affine rings are quotients of finitely generated $\Omega$-algebras). Its unramifiedness and [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] imply every point of $Z_C$ is closed; the closed immersion makes it closed in $C$ as well. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] its underlying subset is finite. Thus $C$ is smooth except at finitely many points, with precisely the local-complete-intersection condition already obtained in step 6. Empty singular set, smooth fibres and disconnected fibres cause no exception.

source.place: Tag 0E00, verifying the isolated-singularity hypothesis of Tag 0DZX.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the open of [lem-sfb-isolated-lci-curve-smooth-open]. Steps 6 and 7, with its field-point characterization, show that every geometric point of $\mathfrak N$ belongs to $\mathcal L_k$. Hence $\mathfrak N$ is an open substack of $\mathcal L_k$: for any scheme-valued object its inverse image of $\mathcal L_k$ is an open containing every geometric point of its base and so is the whole base. Choose a smooth atlas $W\to\mathcal L$ whose composite to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is smooth. Its base change $W_k$ and its open restriction over $\mathfrak N$ have smooth composites to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. On scheme charts this follows from [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] and the locally constant relative-dimension cover in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; open restriction preserves the local lifting condition defining smoothness, since a nilpotent thickening has the same underlying points so its lift still lands in the open. This restricted atlas is surjective, so $\mathfrak N$ is smooth over $k$. Finally all the constructions can be base changed along any field extension $k'/k$: the atlas, the Isom sheaves, and the opens $T_N$ above pull back, and smoothness persists by the same permanence result. This proves every asserted field-extension clause.

source.place: Tag 0E00, proof via Tag 0DZX; base change as in quot.tex remark-curves-base-change.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0DSY and 0E00; algebraicity in quot.tex Tag 0D5A. The nonempty-fibre refinement is the explicit open-image argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q36-bfa71e783 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 11 new unsplit nodes in full, every cited node's statement, and the sources: quot.tex 0D52–0D5A and remark-curves-base-change (l.4497–4830), artin.tex 07Y4 (l.2512), its axioms [-1]–[5], RS, versal and openness-of-versality, moduli-curves 0DSY, 0E00 and 0DZX, spaces-more-morphisms 0DSH, spaces-over-fields 0ADD, spaces-morphisms 042S, and curves definition-nodal, lemma-nodal-family and 0C4E. All tags match their labels. No SGA is cited and there is no repair note. Item statement: against the base, the conventions are written inline (étale stack, representable by algebraic spaces, the same as def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids), and the citation of def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres, which would force connected fibres, is replaced by the inline node condition. The meaning is unchanged and the parent's step 1 still holds. Steps: (1) the descent/Isom node gives the étale stack and diagonal, and the size bound is a set-theoretic triviality. (2) Every 07Y4 premise matches its curve node: limits, RS through a thickening plus affine pushout, tangent/Inf over any field, effectivity for any complete Noetherian local ring, and the identical versality definition; Z is a G-ring. (3) 𝔠 = 𝒞×Spec k, and since U_k×_𝔠 T = U×_𝒞 T the atlas carries over. (4) T_nod = T∖f(X∖V) is open by universal closedness and commutes with base change (Z_{t'} = Z_t⊗κ(t')). Fibre ⊂ V is equivalent to pure dimension 1 and at worst nodal; I checked the generic-point and node-neighbourhood arguments. (5) T_{≠∅} is open by the 042S node; the empty family over a nonempty base is excluded correctly. (6) The 0ADD node makes the fibre a scheme; the 0C4E node with k = Ω gives lci and unramified Sing; 0C3K with d = 1 applies because base changes to larger algebraically closed fields are again geometric fibres. (7) C is Noetherian (pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft); Sing has only closed points (02G7), so it is finite (0BA8 node). (8) The 0DZX clause (3) puts every geometric point of 𝔑 in 𝓛_k, so 𝔑 is open in 𝓛_k and its restricted atlas is smooth over k. New nodes: all are true and self-contained, and none restates the item. lci+ is strictly larger than 𝔑 (cusp, curve⊔point). The space nodal-locus node is not lem-trf-nodal-open-locus (that one is for schemes with pure dimension-1 fibres). 042S generalizes the scheme leaf lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open. Grep found no duplicates. Small cases: empty family over a nonempty base, disconnected smooth curves, nodes in characteristic 2, cusp, curve⊔point, double line. Batch-5 flags: I accept all of them. def-trf-algebraic-space (025Y) is a definition. lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers (02X2), -dth-fitting-smooth-locus (0C3K), -nodal-curve-lci-criterion (0C4E) and -unramified-over-field-local-criterion (02G7) are generic geometry in unit sk-i-curve-zero. The item's closure has 80 trf def/lem nodes and no thm-trf, poincare, trace-transport or batch-4 node, so none of these is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality or their proofs. I accept the declared tool_uses: generic permanence, finiteness and trf lemmas, plus a Mathlib leaf. No fixes.
